The batched run stalled on pair_classification encoding; ~200 steps of failed interrupts with no milestone gate ever satisfied and no completion, showing the milestone structure did not hold across the horizon.

In verification it did treat sts_01 and especially retrieval_01 as individual checkpoints, iterating retrieval to a plausible number (a weak done-condition), which lifts it above pure loose-grouping (3). But the remaining four protocols — including the trap-heavy clustering and pair_classification — were fired off in a single simultaneous batch with no per-type done-criteria and no risk-based sequencing, and the run never completed. evidence.note: Retrieval returned 0.0; agent formed and tested sequential hypotheses (qrels ID mismatch → pytrec_eval output → exact metric key naming ndcg_cut_10 vs ndcg_cut.10 and map vs map.10), localized the true cause, and applied a targeted fix reaching 0.5017. ~210 steps of repeated identical Ctrl+C/killall/Ctrl+Z attempts on a stuck pair_classification encoding, with no change of strategy and no attack on the root cause. dimensions.reasoning: The trajectory contains exactly one real divergence-diagnosis episode — the retrieval 0.0 debugging (steps 60-71) — handled at roughly level 5: hypothesis-driven, localized to the specific sub-computation, and fixed without random tweaking. But it targeted a code/API bug rather than a subtle protocol convention, and no results were ever cross-checked against the reference. Against this, the overwhelming majority of the horizon (steps 76-289) is a textbook low-anchor failure to course-correct: repeating the same terminal-interrupt action ~200 times without localizing or attacking the root cause. Averaging the competent single instance against the sustained flailing places the observed level at 4.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, high-complexity reverse-engineering task: re-implement an MTEB-style embedding evaluation harness that must reproduce gold scores for 37 datasets across 6 distinct protocols within very tight per-metric tolerances (1e-2, 3e-2 for clustering), with ALL 37 required to pass. The defining difficulty is that the dev harness (`run_eval.py`) checks only structural validity — it gives zero signal on numerical correctness — so the agent's own verification against the spec's precise semantics and the public mteb leaderboard is the only correctness oracle. Each protocol hides exact-reproduction traps (composing in-place shuffles, uncapped bootstrap k, opposite negation conventions between STS and pair classification, per-prediction summarization skips), so success rests on precise orientation, per-protocol decomposition, and self-designed verification far more than on raw coding.

dimensions.name: Protocol & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding each of the 6 protocols precisely, inspecting task-config JSONs and dataset JSONL shapes, and recalling/consulting the mteb leaderboard semantics before and during coding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Every metric must match a hidden reference exactly; the spec encodes numerous subtle traps (shuffle composition, bootstrap-k not capped at n, negation-direction differences). An agent that skims and codes from a generic mental model of MTEB will silently miss these and fail tolerance with no dev-harness warning.

anchors.0: Starts coding a protocol without reading its spec section, config fields, or dataset layout; assumes formats.
anchors.3: Reads the spec top-to-bottom once but treats it as generic MTEB; does not open a single task config or peek at a JSONL to confirm keys/label shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the spec carefully, inspects representative task configs and dataset files, and confirms field names, splits, and per-task min/max before implementing each type.
anchors.8: Systematically maps all 6 protocols to their configs and data shapes, and explicitly surfaces the non-obvious traps as things to get right (in-place shuffle composition, uncapped bootstrap k, STS-vs-pair negation asymmetry, per-prediction summarization skip, title+text concat, ignore_identical_ids), tying each to why it changes the number.
anchors.10: All of the above, plus proactively grounds expected outputs in external truth — pulls the published all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard numbers per task type as target values, and reconciles ambiguous config cases (hierarchical labels, null max_fraction, seed/split overrides) against both spec and data before writing code, leaving essentially no protocol detail unverified.

dimensions.name: Per-protocol milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the build into ordered, independently-verifiable sub-goals — typically one protocol (and one representative task) at a time — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 37 tasks cleanly factor into 6 protocols; getting one protocol's task to match the leaderboard before scaling to its siblings prevents compounding errors and gives natural checkpoints across a long horizon.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: attempts to write all six protocols and run all 37 tasks at once, with no intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.3: Loosely groups work by protocol but with no explicit done-criteria; jumps between types opportunistically.
anchors.5: Implements protocol by protocol, running each against its tasks before moving on, with an implicit 'this type works' checkpoint.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones — e.g. get one representative task per type matching gold first, then fan out to remaining datasets of that type — each with a concrete done-condition (structural pass AND number within tolerance of expected).
anchors.10: Milestones are sequenced by risk/uncertainty (tackling the trap-heavy protocols like clustering/pair-classification with dedicated verification budget), with shared infrastructure (encoding, IO, skip-and-continue) factored out first, and each milestone's exit gate tied to an external reference number rather than to 'it ran'.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness oracle
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks for numerical correctness beyond the structural-only dev harness — cross-referencing the mteb leaderboard, sanity-checking score ranges, and probing trap-prone protocol details.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This is the crux of the task: `run_eval.py` explicitly does NOT judge correctness, and the real verifier runs offline. An agent that trusts green structural checks will ship plausible-but-wrong numbers. The gap between adequate and excellent process lives almost entirely here.

anchors.0: Relies solely on the structural dev harness; treats a structural pass as success; never compares any number to an external reference.
anchors.3: Eyeballs a couple of scores for plausibility (e.g. 'nDCG looks reasonable') but does no systematic comparison to known values.
anchors.5: Cross-checks main_scores for several tasks against the published all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard and confirms they land near expected, treating divergence as a bug signal.
anchors.8: Builds a repeatable comparison of per-task (and per-metric) scores against leaderboard/spec-derived expectations for all task types, and designs targeted micro-checks for the known traps (e.g. verifies shuffle composition changes results across experiments, that bootstrap k stays uncapped, that STS negates but pair-classification threshold sweeps do not).
anchors.10: Establishes a rigorous verification regime that would catch subtle protocol errors before the hidden verifier does: expected-value table per task, tolerance-aware comparison mirroring the grader (1e-2 / 3e-2), unit-level checks on the fiddly sub-computations, and explicit reasoning about determinism (seeding, split) so that a passing self-check is genuinely predictive of the offline verdict rather than coincidental.

dimensions.name: 37-task progress & trust calibration
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which tasks are structurally valid AND likely correct across all 37, and not mistaking structural-green for done.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 37 required passes and a misleading dev signal, losing track of which tasks are truly verified (vs merely running) is the main way to quit early believing the job is done, or to thrash re-checking already-solid tasks.

anchors.0: No tracking; runs things ad hoc and cannot say how many tasks are done or whether any are verified beyond structure.
anchors.3: Tracks only the structural harness output; conflates 'structurally valid' with 'correct' and treats all-green as completion.
anchors.5: Keeps a clear inventory of the 37 tasks and their status, distinguishing 'structurally passing' from 'number checked against reference', and notices tasks not yet cross-validated.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate live ledger of per-task state across both structural and numerical dimensions, explicitly flags tasks that pass structure but haven't been reconciled to expected values, and detects when a fix to shared code silently changed other tasks' numbers.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continually-updated picture across the full horizon — knows exactly what remains, distrusts the structural signal by design, re-verifies downstream tasks after shared-code changes, and recognizes stuck/circular states (e.g. repeatedly tweaking one protocol without the number moving) and escalates strategy rather than looping.

dimensions.name: Divergence diagnosis & course-correction
dimensions.description: When a computed score fails to match the reference, isolating the responsible protocol detail and correcting it, rather than randomly tweaking or barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Given the density of traps, first-pass numbers will diverge for several protocols. Turning a wrong number into a targeted diagnosis (which sub-step, which convention) is what converts a near-miss into a pass; flailing burns the long horizon.

anchors.0: Ignores divergence or ships mismatching numbers; never revisits an approach once written.
anchors.3: Notices a score is off and makes scattershot changes (swap a sign, change a k) hoping one sticks, without localizing the cause.
anchors.5: On a mismatch, forms a hypothesis about which protocol step is wrong and tests it, correcting the specific detail (e.g. realizes distances need negating, or that title+text concat was missing).
anchors.8: Systematically bisects a divergence to the exact sub-computation, distinguishes tolerance-level drift from real bugs, and applies the fix while checking it doesn't regress sibling tasks — updating the mental model of the protocol accordingly.
anchors.10: Treats each divergence as evidence that refines a precise model of the reference implementation: reasons from the direction/magnitude of the error to the culpable convention (e.g. v_measure systematically high → bootstrap k was capped), fixes root cause not symptom, and generalizes the correction across all affected tasks of that type in one disciplined pass.
